newsitem.title: GERMANY: Crest head says determined to meet April deadline.
newsitem.headline: Crest head says determined to meet April deadline.

text.p: Crest, Britain's fledgling electronic share registration system, is already handling 40 percent of market transactions in domestic stocks and is on track to be fully on stream next April, its developers said on Thursday.

Despite complaints from users about delays and software problems with Crest, which started its transition phase in August, its developers told a Frankfurt business seminar they were determined to meet the April deadline for full operation.

"What we have done is go from nothing to sales via Crest amounting to 40 percent of the market -- a size about as large as many other equity markets in full -- so it's not surprising people are feeling the strain," said Iain Saville, chief executive of development group CrestCo.

Saville and his team said some 1,000 U.K. securities now were held on the paperless Crest system, representing a volume of some 313 billion pounds ($508 billion), or a third of the market's total capitalisation.
The system has 246 users (banks and brokerages who control the transfers) and 1,099 participants (who actually own the securities), numbers which are expected to rise significantly.

Saville said he would not be moved to delay Crest's schedule to give users and companies more time to adapt to the new paperless environment and said some problems were due to brokers' inabilty to adapt to a new regime.
"We want to get this out of the way so that we can get on to other things -- like preparing for EMU. If it causes a bit of pain for some, then so be it," he said.
With Crest, shares no longer have a share certificate but instead, owners of shares are listed in company registers which are linked to Crest and are informed regularly on share transfers.

The system is a voluntary alternative to paper settlement but so far 75 percent of the outstanding shares in the companies involved have been transferred to the system and Saville said he was confident that amount would grow.
Many of the initial problems with Crest were already easing significantly, he said.
"Three weeks ago only 60 percent of transactions were settling on the intended date but now it is 79 percent, which is also poor, but around the same as in Talisman (the existing system)," he said.
In Frankfurt to talk to his counterparts in the German securities industry, Saville said he hoped for closer co-operation with other settlement systems in Europe in the future.
He also said he aimed in the long term to use Crest as a basis for consolidating the different securities systems in the U.K., creating a unified system for stocks and government and corporate bonds.
Saville concluded: "This (Crest) is a strategic vehicle capable of supporting the U.K.'s role in financial services in the future." ($1=.6161 Pound)
